blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Signs Your Elgin Main Line Needs Rodding
blocks.intro: A single slow sink is one thing. These point to the main:

tiles.body: The floor drain is the lowest point in most Elgin basements. A main line clog shows up there first.

tiles.h3: Toilets Bubble When the Tub Drains
tiles.body: Air being pushed back through other fixtures means the line ahead is blocked.
A washer empties a lot of water fast. A partly blocked main can't keep up and overflows downstairs.

tiles.h3: It Was Rodded About a Year Ago
tiles.body: In older clay lines, roots grow back on a yearly cycle.

blocks.h2: What Blocks Main Lines in Elgin
blocks.intro: With homes from the 1800s through the 2000s, we clear every kind of main line clog in Elgin.

items.body: In the older neighborhoods east of the river, roots grow into clay joints and form dense mats. Rodding cuts them back so water flows again.

items.h3: Rust Scale in Cast Iron Stacks
items.body: Older homes often have cast iron inside the house. Scale builds on the walls and narrows the pipe.

items.h3: Wipes and Grease in Newer Homes
items.body: On the west side, most main line clogs come from what goes down the drain, not the pipe itself.
Roots that return within months call for [hydro jetting](/elgin/hydro-jetting). A crack or sag on camera means a [sewer repair](/elgin/sewer-repair).

blocks.intro: Clear the line, then show you why it clogged.

steps.body: We locate the cleanout, protect the floor and set up there, not through a toilet if we can avoid it.
We rod to the city main and follow with a camera so you see the cause and what's left.
You get the price first. If the camera shows damage, you get options and a price for each.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Elgin Homeowners

items.q: How do I know the clog is in the main line?
items.preview: Several fixtures are slow, or water shows up at the floor drain.
items.answer: If more than one fixture is slow, toilets gurgle when other drains run or water appears at the basement floor drain, the clog is in the main line rather than one fixture.

items.q: How often should an Elgin home with roots be rodded?
items.preview: Usually once a year, before spring.
items.answer: If roots have blocked your line before, once a year is a good starting point, ideally in late winter or early spring before roots grow and storms test the line.

items.q: Will rodding hurt my old clay pipe?
items.preview: Not when it's done right. The camera shows if the pipe is already broken.
items.answer: Not when the cutting head is sized correctly. If the line is already cracked or collapsed, the camera will show it, and we'll stop and explain before going further.

items.q: Can I rent a machine and do it myself?
items.preview: You can, but you won't see what caused it.
items.answer: You can rent a machine, but heavy cables are hard to control, and you won't know what caused the clog or whether the pipe is damaged. Our camera follow-up answers that.

items.q: How much does sewer rodding cost in Elgin?
items.preview: It depends on access and the blockage. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the cleanout is, how long the line is and what's in it. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
